get.description:
Search over the directory of users by name, email address or phone number. By name it is fuzzy: any word of the name, typos, similar sounding names and any script (a Cyrillic name finds its Latin spelling and the reverse). An email address or a phone number is looked up exactly. Each result carries a `confidence`, the similarity of the query to the name computed from the strings alone; it is a measure of likeness, not the probability that this is the right person. A service token without a company searches the whole directory; any other token is limited to its own company, and naming another company is rejected.

### Allowed Auth Scopes

- messaging:SearchUsers
- messaging:read

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the tenant when a service token is used.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to look for: a name as typed or as a speech recognizer heard it, an email address, or a phone number. Required: a request without it is rejected with a `ValidationException`. It is not marked required in the model because a required query parameter becomes part of the route, and a request without it would answer 404 instead.

schema.description: What to look for: a name as typed or as a speech recognizer heard it, an email address, or a phone number. Required: a request without it is rejected with a `ValidationException`. It is not marked required in the model because a required query parameter becomes part of the route, and a request without it would answer 404 instead.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: How `q` is read. `auto` (default) takes `q` for an email address when it contains `@` (looked up exactly, so a malformed one matches nobody), for a phone number when it is a number with its country code (`+` and digits, grouped by spaces, `-`, `.`, `/` or brackets as written), and for a name otherwise. A number of seven or more digits without its country code is refused with a `ValidationException`: numbers are stored in E.164, so it would match nobody. `name`, `email` and `phone` force the reading and refuse input that cannot be it. An email or phone lookup is exact and gives every result a `confidence` of 1. `kind`, `withExtensionOnly` and `minConfidence` apply in every mode.

id.description: A unique ID of the action within the message.

channelId.description: Direct-channel ids are the 8-4-4-4-8 slices of the two member ids. An `a_` member id puts `_` in a slice, so the pattern allows it.

channelVersion.description: Channel version. Increments on every channel mutation.

lastActivityAt.description: Timestamp of the last activity. Drives inbox ordering.

pinnedMessageIds.description: Message ids currently pinned at channel scope, newest pin first. Empty when nothing is pinned.

peerId.description: Direct channels only: the other member's user id, relative to the caller. Absent for group channels and for direct channels that do not have exactly two members.

picture.description: The URL of the channel's picture.

pictureColor.description: The dominant color of the channel's picture, represented by a hex value.

broadcast.description: Indicates if the channel is broadcast-only. Default is false.

sms.description: Indicates if the channel supports SMS. Default is false.

mms.description: Indicates if the channel supports MMS. Default is false.

whatsapp.description: Indicates if the channel supports WhatsApp. Default is false.

kiteAssign.description: The unique identifier of the assignee.

autoRecord.description: Indicates if the channel supports auto start recording.

autoTranscribe.description: Indicates if a conference in the channel starts transcription automatically. When absent, clients follow autoRecord, which used to start both recording and transcription.

wizyGuestViewOnly.description: Indicates if external users in this conversation can only join the conference as a viewer with the ability to speak by request. Default is false.

messagingSenderId.description: The business side of the conversation: the Facebook Page ID on Messenger, the Instagram account ID on Instagram, the brand id on RCS. A reply has to name the sender it is sent from. On Messenger and Instagram kite writes it from the inbound event, because the channel id hashes the sender's linked service and not the sender; on RCS the channel id includes the brand, and it is written when the channel is created.

messagingReplyUntil.description: Epoch seconds until which a reply still reaches the person. On Messenger and Instagram this is Meta's 7 day HUMAN_AGENT deadline, restarted by each inbound message; classound applies the tag itself, so this is the one deadline a client has to show. 0 means the deadline is not known, which is what the inbound event carries when the session row was gone before it could be read back; it does not mean the window has closed, so a client reads the window as closed on `messagingReplyUntil > 0 && now > messagingReplyUntil` and shows nothing at 0. Absent on a channel with no reply window.

broadcastId.description: A unique identifier of x-hoppers broadcast conference. If present x-hoppers application will use broadcast and push-to-talk functionality for the channel.

ChannelMessagingStatus.description: Set when classound refused a reply because the person's messaging window is closed (a 409 on the send). Unset by the next inbound message, which is the only thing that reopens the window.

ChatVerbosity.description: How much of a chat turn x-bees shows while the agent works. SMS and WhatsApp always send one final text.

LastMessagePreview.description: Preview of the most recent visible message in a channel.

text.description: Text body of the message. Absent for attachment-only or deleted messages.

pollId.description: Poll identifier when the message is a poll, so a preview can be rendered as one. Absent for a deleted message; the poll body is not stored.

event.description: System event identifier for client rendering.

text.description: Text body. Empty for attachment-only or deleted messages.

mentions.description: Users directly mentioned in the message.

pinnedBy.description: User that pinned the message. Absent when not pinned.

system.description: True when the message is system-generated.

MessageMessagingStatus.description: The delivery state of a message an x-bees user sent over a customer messaging channel (see MessagingChannel), the same four states as WhatsApp. TRYING, SENT and ERROR are written by kite around the send; DELIVERED and a late ERROR arrive through the channel's status stream event (MESSENGER.STATUS, RCS.STATUS). A READ report is recorded as DELIVERED, as the WhatsApp producer does one hop earlier.

An RCS conversation is not a telephony channel, and its customer id is the person's phone number.

highlights.description: Highlighted fragments from the matched channel subject or description.

results.description: Matching messages, access-filtered and ordered by the requested sort.

totalCount.description: Total OpenSearch hit count before the visibility post-filter; approximate.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Absent when there are no more pages.

confidence.description: Similarity of a query to a name, from 0 (nothing in common) to 1 (the same words). Depends only on the two strings, not on the size of the company.

SearchUsersKind.description: Which users a user search is run among.

SearchUsersMode.description: How the query of a user search is read.

results.description: Matching users ordered by descending confidence.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Absent when there are no more pages.

margin.description: Confidence of the first result minus that of the second in this response. Absent when fewer than two results remain. A large margin means the first result stands out; a small one means the answer is ambiguous.

StreamUser.description: A user of the directory. Every field except `id`, `displayName` and `bot` is present only when the directory holds it and the caller may see it.

displayName.description: What to call the user: their name, or when they have none the part of their email before the @, or when they have neither their id. Always present.

bot.description: True when the user is a bot.

pbxExtension.description: Extension on the PBX the user is linked to.

locale.description: Language of the user's client, as a locale tag.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the user.

deactivatedAt.description: When the user was deactivated. Absent for an active user.

updatedAt.description: When the directory entry of the user was last written.

UserMatchedOn.description: Which kind of match carried a search hit.

WilmaChatArtifact.description: An artifact the turn shared. The files stay in the artifacts store; `artifactId` opens it.

WilmaChatElement.description: On every agent reply of a Wilma chat on the stream transport: the session and turn that produced it, how the turn went and what it shared. `verbosity` is the agent's setting when the session started; clients decide from it what to show. The turn's events are `startIndex`..`endIndex` of the session log: read them with GetSessionEvents(sessionId, startIndex).

turn.description: The turn of the session that produced this message. A steer that joins a running turn shares it.

startIndex.description: Index of the turn's first event (`turnStarted`) in the session log.

endIndex.description: Index of the turn's last event (completed, failed or stopped). Absent when the message was written before the turn ended.

WilmaChatTurnSummary.description: How the turn went. The calls themselves (input, output) are not stored here: they are the turn's events in the session log.

durationMs.description: From the turn's start to its end. Absent when the turn had not ended.

toolCount.description: Steps the turn took, counted as the Wilma assistant counts its work steps: each tool call and each sandbox step (`SandboxStartedEvent`, `SandboxFailedEvent`).

failedCount.description: Steps that failed: calls that failed, including those the stop or failure cut off, and sandbox steps that failed.
